paper_findings.paper: FlyRank - The State of AI-Driven SEO in Numbers, March 2026 data report
paper_findings.scope: 341,701 content pieces, 57 brands; aggregate comparisons primary, ML appendix exploratory

finding_1.name: ML appendix - RF feature importance for the health score

paper_numbers.health_score_composition: impressions 30 pts + position 30 pts + ctr 20 pts + scroll depth 20 pts

finding_1.paper_disclosure: the target itself is partly constructed from some of these inputs; importance is descriptive rather than causal
finding_1.my_question: label provenance: importance ranking over the label's own ingredients is close to mechanical - what survives a train-without-those-ingredients test, or a score-free outcome label?
finding_1.where_i_test_it: section 3 of this notebook (train-with / train-without confessions on my own features)

finding_2.name: ML appendix - logistic-regression growth prediction, 71% holdout accuracy

paper_numbers.ml_sample: 61.8K content pieces with sessions > 0 and impressions > 0
paper_numbers.full_sample_growth_mix: about 74.2K rising vs 45.3K falling (~62% majority class)

finding_2.paper_disclosure: no p-values or confidence intervals reported; observational study; ML pages exploratory and secondary
finding_2.my_question: validation design: (1) print the grow/decline base rate next to the accuracy - 71% on a ~62% base rate is ~9 skill points; (2) does the 71% survive a brand-grouped (or age-matched) holdout, given random 80/20 lets one brand's pages sit in train and test?
finding_2.where_i_test_it: sections 2-3 of this notebook (my model: random split vs client-grouped, base rate on every metric)

before_after.stability_note: grouped metrics are order-stable (GroupKFold assigns clients deterministically; reproduced to the digit across reruns); the shuffled/dishonest row is order-sensitive (KFold fixes positions over a parallel-GROUP-BY frame order) and wobbles between runs - labeled exhibit, never a claim

timeline_strict.evidence: feature window max 2026-03-20 <= decision 2026-03-20 < label window min 2026-03-21..2026-03-31 <= 03-31

meta_date_neutralized.evidence: 67,109/83,258 pages (80.6%) have meta_unknown=1 forcing meta_stale_days=0; no post-decision date reaches a feature

no_label_siblings.evidence: label-window columns ['target_mean', 'decline_11d'] absent from the 21-feature matrix (name scan: none; direct scan: none)

confession_test.evidence: with 'target_mean' + 'label_ratio' added to features, grouped OOF AUC jumps 0.659 -> 1.000; removed afterwards

no_product_flags.evidence: no existing-system scores in features (scan ['health_score', 'flag_summary', 'optimization_flag', 'internal_score', 'ai_flag', 'traffic_flag']: none); constructed flags ['ctr_fix_flag'] built from <= 03-20 page data only (construction receipted in w05)

population_disclosed.evidence: page-keeping uses outcome-window info: 314 pages absent from the 03-21..31 window are dropped (aggregates-only), plus pace>0 (n=37) - disclosed as a choice in w05 and here (mortality-selection caveat)

grouped_split.evidence: every grouped fold train/test client-disjoint (receipt printed in sec 2)

base_rate.evidence: base rate 15.9% printed in the sec-2 table beside every AUC/P@K

top_feature_sane.evidence: w05 permutation top = 'momentum_capped' (roc_auc drop ~0.033), top standardized coef 'momentum_capped' +0.276 - matches audited lane directions; honest AUC 0.659 is far from 'suspiciously perfect'

oof_metrics.evidence: all sec-3 honest scores are OOF under the same folds (assert np.isfinite(...).all())

claims.as_written: Momentum CONFIRMED as the main risk signal (+0.107 after a 2-slice audit).
claims.rewrite: Measured: momentum showed the largest single-axis and permutation association with 11-day decline in this lane's audits (single-axis AUC 0.585; grouped-OOF model leans on it first). Directional, observed on one month's mid-panel and one 11-day label - it raises review priority; it is not evidence that momentum CAUSES decline.
claims.licensed_by: single-axis AUC 0.585 + w05 permutation top_lever = momentum_capped

claims.as_written: The model ranks decline risk better than the hand rule overall.
claims.rewrite: Measured on the same grouped-OOF evaluation: AUC 0.659 vs 0.544 and P@20 0.55 vs 0.35 (base rate 15.9%). Decision-support: the model changes which ~20 pages a reviewer reads first in this slice; it is not a validated production lift and says nothing about pages outside this population.
claims.licensed_by: w05 comparison_table: LR AUC 0.659/P@20 0.55 vs rule AUC 0.544/P@20 0.35 (same-data receipt)

claims.as_written: The CTR-fix flag is a confirmed signal at the 11-day horizon (+11.0 / +7.7 / +7.3 pp across the top three position bands).
claims.rewrite: Observed: within this slice, low band-relative CTR (the flag) co-occurred with larger 11-day declines in the audited position bands (each band n >= 30, per the study's own floor discipline). Directional - it marks a page for a click-capture review; the measured gaps are slice-conditional, and the flag's construction receipt (band medians, <= 03-20 only) bounds what it can claim.
claims.licensed_by: w04 CTR-fix slice receipts (top-3/4-10/11-30, n>=30) + w05 coef ctr_fix_flag +0.074

claims.as_written: Random Forest's complexity did not earn its keep.
claims.rewrite: Measured: under the same client-grouped OOF protocol, the RF's mean fold AUC matched the LR's (0.657 vs 0.656) but its P@20 was 0.25 vs 0.55 - no top-of-queue gain to offset the loss of readable coefficients. Decision-support wording: on this slice, no measured benefit bought the complexity; revisit if features or slice change.
claims.licensed_by: w05 comparison_table RF row + fold_auc receipt

claim_rewrite.rule: no claim goes further than its receipt; every rewrite keeps its anchoring number and its slice bounds
